rubric: This is a livestream transcript (IRL, just chatting or gaming streamers). A great clip is a REACTION moment or a bit: what just happened or what they were trying (the setup that makes it land), then the reaction itself (shock, rage, hype, laughter, a roast), ending once it has landed. A short story the streamer tells with a punchline also works. Reject reading chat out loud, thanking donations and subs, idle commentary, setting up the stream and technical downtime. A 💬 after the time marks a sentence where Twitch chat blew up in the seconds just after it (spam, KEKW/LUL, CLIP IT) - a strong hint the reaction landed. Judge by meaning; 💬 is a signal, not a guarantee.
outline: A topic is one event or bit: one encounter, one round or attempt, one story, one conversation with chat or a guest about one thing. A new topic starts when the streamer moves on (next game, next person, next video, "alright chat"). Reading donations, alerts and dead air belong to no topic.
review: A stream clip needs the setup a cold viewer must see to get the reaction, and ends once the reaction has landed: not on the streamer turning back to chat, reading a donation, or starting the next thing.
